newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end up but gains capped by rate concerns.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end up but gains capped by rate concerns.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended modestly higher on Wednesday, with gains in Cheung Kong shares and some property counters providing the market with a lift but interest rate concerns capping the upside, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index closed 34.77 points higher at 13,454.93 after rising to a session high of 13,501.19.
Turnover was HK$11.37 billion compared with HK$13.57 billion on Tuesday.
"Cheung Kong is doing the whole thing," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities, of the Hang Seng's rise.
Cheung Kong shares ended with a gain of HK$2.00 at HK$74.75. Cheung Kong Infrastructure rose HK$0.50 to HK$21.75.
But Galbraith said a continued rise in the U.S. long bond yield and caution ahead of the release of key U.S. economic statistics this week had kept the Hang Seng in a narrow range.

"If one or two (figures) are a bit too inflationary then I expect the market to have some kind of correction, especially since the long bond yield is over 6.7 percent which is a bit worrying," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond fell 7/32 overnight to yield 6.79 percent.
Chan said figures showing a stronger-than-expected U.S. economy could prompt a correction in Hong Kong stocks but added the Hang Seng index should find support around 13,000 points.
"I think it (the range) will be narrow ahead of the employment numbers in the States," said Howard Gorges, a director at South China Brokerage.
The December U.S. jobs report is due on Friday.
Gorges said there had been some profit-taking in the general market on Wednesday following a 221 point surge in the Hang Seng on Monday, and H-shares and red chips had come under pressure.
The H-share index closed 28.94 points lower at 1,005.92.
Among the red chips, China Resources finished HK$0.60 lower at HK$16.75 and China Travel fell HK$0.175 to HK$3.575.
CITIC Pacific rose HK$0.50 to HK$39.70 after shedding HK$1.00 on Tuesday and HK$1.40 on Monday.
Hutchison and Hongkong Electric also ran into profit-taking. Hutchison slipped HK$0.75 to HK$60.50 and Hongkong Electric fell HK$0.50 to HK$27.15.
Henderson Land rose HK$1.25 to HK$76.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.00 to HK$95.25.
